```python
# tests/test_items.py
def test_array_slice_deletion_keeps_render_in_sync() -> None:
    # Regression: deleting a slice must keep as_string() consistent with the
    # list contents. Slices with stop == 0 or negative bounds previously
    # corrupted the rendered array (e.g. `del a[:0]` wiped every element).
    a = item([1, 2, 3])
    del a[:0]  # deletes nothing
    assert a == [1, 2, 3]
    assert a.as_string() == "[1, 2, 3]"

    a = item([1, 2, 3])
    del a[-1:]
    assert a == [1, 2]
    assert a.as_string() == "[1, 2]"

    a = item([1, 2, 3])
    del a[:-1]
    assert a == [3]
    assert a.as_string() == "[3]"
```

```python
    def as_string(self) -> str:
        if not self._multiline or not self._value:
            rendered = list(self._iter_items())
            inner = "".join(v.as_string() for v in rendered)
            if rendered and isinstance(rendered[-1], Comment):
                # A trailing comment (e.g. from add_line(comment=...)) carries
                # no newline, so keep the closing bracket off the comment line
                # to produce parseable output (GH #580).
                inner += "\n" + self.trivia.indent
            return f"[{inner}]"

        s = "[\n"
        s += "".join(
            self.trivia.indent
            + " " * 4
            + v.value.as_string()
            + ("," if not isinstance(v.value, Null) else "")
            + (v.comment.as_string() if v.comment is not None else "")
            + "\n"
            for v in self._value
            if v.value is not None
        )
        s += self.trivia.indent + "]"

        return s
```
